# PSY Psykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Svendborg)

PSY Psykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Svendborg) is a psychiatric outpatient clinic in Denmark that appears in the corpus as a reporting unit in the Danish ADHD quality database (ADHD-databasen), as documented in the 2024 ADHD annual report [^src1][^src2]. The clinic is cited twice in connection with two different quality indicators tracked at the department level.

The clinic's most notable appearance is in connection with **Indicator 10**, which measures the share of adult ADHD treatment courses in which a patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of starting treatment [^src1]. According to the source table, the clinic recorded "Nej 17 / 127 13 (8-21)" — meaning it did not meet the quality target, with 17 out of 127 treatment courses meeting the criterion, corresponding to 13% (confidence interval 8–21%) [^src1]. This places PSY Psykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Svendborg) among the lowest-performing units on this measure, which is significant because Indicator 10 was reported for the first time in the 2024 ADHD database, and both the national target of 90% and the actual national result of 37% were badly missed, with regional results ranging from 14% to 52% [^src1]. The steering group behind the database discussed possible causes for the widespread shortfall, including registration practices and data quality issues from child/adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and resolved to work on improving registration practices [^src1].

The clinic is also listed in connection with a second, higher figure: "65 / 127 51 (42-60)", indicating 65 out of 127 cases meeting the relevant criterion, or 51% (confidence interval 42–60%) [^src2]. This appears in the section of the report covering **Indicator 11**, which measures the share of adult treatment courses in which the patient was receiving ADHD medication within 120 days of starting a structured treatment package (pakkeforløb) — an indicator reported for adults for the first time in 2024, following the database's expansion to include adult patients that year [^src2]. The broader context shows substantial regional variation on this indicator nationally, from 85% in Region Nordjylland to 37% in Region Hovedstaden, a spread the report attributes mainly to differences in registration practice rather than genuine clinical variation [^src2].

No relationships to other named entities and no separately extracted claims are recorded for this clinic in the corpus beyond the two indicator results above.
